features.description: `git forge pr merge --ff` executes a fast-forward: result_commit == source_head (no new commit, single-parent chain preserved); precondition merge_base == base_head; before #2 lands, a moved base refuses naming recreate-or-rebase-and-recheck; after #2, the ff gate revalidates against the live-base result.
expectedBehavior: `pr merge --ff` on a strictly-on-top source exits zero; `pr show` displays result_commit == source_head; the integrated base tip's parent is the prior base tip (no merge commit)
Non-ffable PR + `--ff`: exits non-zero with a distinct error naming the rebase remedy; no ref change; PR remains unmerged
Moved base (current base != snapshot base_head, pre-#2): refuses naming recreate-or-rebase-and-recheck; base/PR refs unchanged
CAS clash injected (base advanced between expectation check and finalize): merge fails, no partial write (base/PR/issue refs all unchanged) — exact-base CAS holds
Existing merge strategies unchanged: merge-commit/squash/rebase paths byte-identical in behavior
gf-dogfood.sh gains --ff assertions (success + non-ff refusal)

features.description: Relax the checked-out base guard: `pr merge` succeeds while base_ref is checked out in a non-temporary worktree, provided that worktree is clean; after the base CAS, the base worktree is refreshed to the result commit. Refresh failure exits non-zero with refs unchanged (no partial move) and reports the worktree as a leftover.
expectedBehavior: Clean main-tree base (base_ref checked out, `git status --porcelain` empty): merge exits zero; after merge the worktree files match the result commit and the tree is clean
Dirty base (modified tracked file AND untracked file cases): merge exits non-zero, base ref value unchanged; untracked counts as dirty
Ignored-only dirt: merge proceeds (ignored does NOT count as dirty)
Refresh-failure injection: merge exits non-zero, base ref and worktree HEAD agree (no partial move), output reports the worktree as a leftover
docs/architecture/git-forge.md: guard section updated; Known Limitations names sparse-checkout and submodules as out of L1 scope
gf-dogfood.sh: refusal-on-checked-out-base assertions reversed; clean-merge/dirty-refusal assertions added

features.description: `git forge pr merge <n> --recycle-worktree <path>` removes the merged source worktree and conditionally deletes its branch, returning a structured outcome line for orchestrators. Runs after base refresh (#3) and finalization; never touches the base worktree; salvage renaming of unmerged branches is pipeline-side and happens BEFORE this call.
expectedBehavior: Clean registered source worktree, checked-out branch == PR source_ref, `--ff` merge: worktree removed (absent from `git worktree list`), branch deleted, outcome `removed` + `branch-deleted`
Unregistered path or worktree not on the PR source_ref: exits non-zero, outcome `refused-not-contained`, refs unchanged, the referenced worktree is untouched
Dirty source worktree without `--force`: exits non-zero, outcome `refused-dirty`, worktree and branch intact; with `--force`: proceeds
`--squash`/`--rebase` merge with recycle: branch kept, outcome `branch-kept(<reason>)` naming why; `--ff`/`--merge` delete the branch
Partial-removal injection: outcome `partial-leftover(<path>)` naming the path
Base worktree untouched by recycle: after a merge with recycle, the base worktree is clean and at the result commit
Switchover ordering contract held: #9/#3/#4 landed by the old path (no forge PR) and the announcement lives in this ticket's OLD-PATH integration commit message + Issue comment
gf-dogfood.sh covers the outcome vocabulary (removed / refused-dirty / refused-not-contained / branch-deleted / branch-kept)

features.description: Implement the eight-clause adapter contract inside `devflow.cjs` behind `propose --forge`: PR creation at merge-gate time, idempotent issue projection, proof-ticket closure, failure taxonomy, crash reconcile/resume probe, recycle ownership consuming #4's structured outcome, progress-log mirroring, and a fake git-forge test-matrix fixture with dual-path parity.
expectedBehavior: `propose --forge` creates PRs at merge-gate time; `runtime.json` gains prId/issueId; progress log records `forge_pr_created`
Filing is idempotent: a retry reuses the open Issue matched by `session:<s>` label + first body line `Ticket: <fid>` — forge-side issue count does not grow across retries
Proof tickets close via exactly one issue comment (evidence pointer + status) + close; all forge write calls originate from the adapter, never validators

Failure taxonomy maps each class to its named pause/recreate path: ci red→`gate_failed`; stale/superseded→recreate (`forge_pr_superseded`, no pause); bridge/parse + persistent CAS→RECOVERABLE `forge_bridge_failed`; recycle refused/partial→`worktree_partial_removal`
Crash reconcile probe converges all three injected interrupt states (merged-not-recorded / merged-open-issue / merged-remaining-worktree) and never re-invokes `pr merge`
Recycle ownership: adapter consumes #4's structured outcome, runs salvage BEFORE recycle, persists the outcome before clearing feature.worktree/branch
Fake git-forge fixture + dual-path parity green in the implement-skill test matrix; progress-log mirror events reconstruct the recreate window
